name: Estonia

findings.local_actor: Elisa Eesti AS; Government of Estonia
findings.reversal_of: Huawei radio equipment in Elisa Eesti's 2G–5G networks
findings.summary: Under Estonia's prior-authorisation regime for network equipment, a 2022 government order classed Huawei as high-risk and gave Elisa only time-limited permits: Huawei gear allowed in 5G until end-2025 and in 2G–4G until end-2029.
findings.analyst_inference: Reversal tier 5: Huawei equipment was operating in Elisa's network. Enabling law: May 2020 Electronic Communications Act amendment letting government set by regulation which devices may be used (ERR 2020). Elisa challenged the order; Tallinn Administrative Court referred case C-354/24 to the CJEU; AG Ćapeta's non-binding opinion of 19 March 2026 found such restrictions justifiable without compensation. Final judgment not seen. Whether Elisa met the end-2025 5G deadline not confirmed.

findings.summary: Elisa Estonia chose Nokia under a five-year deal to supply its nationwide 5G network, replacing its 4G network equipment, with rollout expected in 2022; Elisa has since replaced most of its Huawei equipment with Nokia.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: Nokia is Finnish. Contract date not given in the opened page (rollout expected 2022), so date null. Tier 3 coded for the contract; Telecoms.com's statement that most Huawei kit was replaced suggests operation at scale, but no deployment figures seen. Value undisclosed.

findings.summary: Tele2 picked Nokia as its 5G radio access partner across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, and as primary vendor for standalone 5G core and voice-over-5G, including Estonia.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third (Finnish vendor). Single opened source. Light Reading does not say whether Tele2 Estonia previously used Huawei RAN; legacy vendor not established. Value undisclosed.

findings.summary: Telia signed group deals in November 2025 naming Ericsson for radio access in Estonia and Nokia for its 5G standalone core there; Telia's Estonian 5G network launched in 2020 was already Ericsson-built.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: both vendors are Swedish/Finnish. Values undisclosed. Estonian World supports only the 2020 Ericsson build, not the 2025 deal; the 2025 contract details rest on DCD.

findings.summary: Greenergy is expanding its Hüüru data centre near Tallinn, Estonia's largest, by 22MW (to 31.5MW) for AI workloads, with Nebius deploying AI cloud infrastructure; first phase due to operate in late 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic: owner-operator Greenergy is owned by MCF Group Estonia, with Estonian private investors (IntelliNews). Tenant Nebius (Amsterdam-headquartered, Nasdaq-listed) would be pole third for its cloud/compute but is a tenant here. Tier 4 because a main contractor is appointed and investment committed; construction start not explicitly dated. US$58m is DCD's conversion of a locally reported EUR 50m expansion; IntelliNews reports total investment of nearly EUR 200m by end-2026. GPU type undisclosed.

findings.controller: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking / LUMI AI Factory consortium (CSC, Finland)
findings.local_actor: ETAIS / University of Tartu (Estonian consortium partner)
findings.financier: EuroHPC JU (Digital Europe Programme) 50%; LUMI AI Factory consortium 50%
findings.summary: Estonia is one of six countries in the LUMI AI Factory consortium; EuroHPC signed a EUR 387.8m contract with Bull in August 2026 for the LUMI-AI supercomputer at CSC's Kajaani site in Finland, due 2027.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: facility is in Finland, operated by CSC and controlled by EuroHPC and the consortium, not by Estonia alone. Estonia's own financial share not stated; the EUR 387.8m is the whole contract (half EuroHPC, half consortium), so values left null. Accelerators are AMD Instinct MI430X (US silicon), supplied via Bull (France); not coded as an Estonian silicon finding because the system sits outside Estonia.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Education and Research; AI Leap Foundation
findings.summary: Estonia's AI Leap (TI-Hüpe) programme gives upper-secondary students and teachers AI learning tools; announced February 2025 with OpenAI and Anthropic negotiations, its 2025–26 pilot covers 154 schools and 20,000 students using OpenAI and Google technology.

sources.publisher: Estonian Ministry of Education and Research

findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 (pilot). The ministry release and Euronews describe negotiations with OpenAI and Anthropic, with OpenAI saying it would bring ChatGPT Edu; the April 2026 state factsheet names only OpenAI and Google, not Anthropic, and describes an Estonian-language app built on their technology, so pole us via provider service. Anthropic's final role unconfirmed. Pilot budget EUR 4m, half ministry and half private (incl. Telia); not converted. Expansion to 38,000 more learners planned 2026–27.

findings.local_actor: RIA, Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs
findings.summary: RIA runs Bürokratt, a round-the-clock Estonian-language virtual assistant for public-service questions that hands users over to human staff, and is developing rules and tools for secure public-sector use of autonomous AI assistants.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic: RIA develops and operates the service. Underlying model or provider not stated on the page, so a foreign model dependency cannot be excluded. Tier 5 assumes the service described as existing runs nationally; launch date not given. Source date is the page's last update.

silicon.null_reason: no in-country accelerator purchase found; Nebius GPU type at Hüüru undisclosed; LUMI-AI AMD GPUs sit in Finland

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced; Sunly AI data centre lead not followed
